children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're enquiring about, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'd like to check if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - Alex, who's 16 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! Since Alex is 16 years old, I have a few more questions to help determine your eligibility.

Is Alex currently in full-time non-advanced education (such as A-levels, NVQs up to level 3, or similar) or on an approved training course?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in college or anything like that at the moment. They actually left school recently and just signed up with the local careers service to figure out what they want to do next.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. That's helpful to know.

When Alex registered with the local careers service, was this through an official government-approved body or scheme for young people? For example, in England this might be through the Connexions service or a similar careers guidance organisation that works with young people who are not in education, employment or training.

Also, could you tell me approximately how long ago Alex left school and registered with the careers service?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, it was through the official careers service in our area - you know, the one that helps young people sort out their next steps after school. It was quite recent actually, just a few weeks ago when they left school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Based on what you've told me, this is very relevant to your situation.

I have a couple more questions to confirm eligibility:

1. Are you living in the UK?
2. Does Alex live with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're in Manchester. And yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. Just one more question to make sure I have the full picture:

Has Alex started any paid work of 24 hours or more per week, or are they receiving any benefits in their own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't working at all at the moment, and they're not getting any benefits themselves either.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for all that information. I now have everything I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:

- You live in the UK (Manchester)
- Alex is 16 years old and lives with you
- Alex recently left school and has registered with an official government-sponsored careers service
- Alex is not working 24+ hours per week
- Alex is not receiving any benefits in their own right

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! Based on the information you've provided, **you are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of why:

**For Alex (age 16):**
- Although Alex has left school and isn't currently in education or training, they have registered with an official government-sponsored careers service
- Under Child Benefit rules, when a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and registers with a government-sponsored careers service, you can continue to receive Child Benefit for **up to 20 weeks** from the date of registration
- Alex lives with you in the UK, isn't working 24+ hours per week, and isn't claiming benefits in their own right

**Important things to note:**
- This 20-week extension period starts from when Alex registered with the careers service
- If Alex starts approved education or training, an apprenticeship, paid work of 24+ hours per week, or begins claiming certain benefits during this period, your eligibility may change
- You should notify the Child Benefit Office of any changes in circumstances

If you have any further questions about your claim, please don't hesitate to ask!
